The rep never anchors a bill or digs into the customer's stated motivation, but he holds the qualification sequence together and locks a specific day and time despite three reschedule attempts. Ending on an unresolved caller-ID/spam concern leaves a legitimacy question open for the specialist's call.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: proactive caller-ID disclosure to protect the sit
primary_coaching_focus.quote: It's just because, like, I get so much so many, like, random ass phone calls, you know, that I don't answer.
primary_coaching_focus.why: This customer flagged, in his own words, exactly the failure mode that kills a booked appointment: an unrecognized number he won't pick up. The rep only addressed it because the customer asked; on the next call where a customer doesn't think to ask, this appointment quietly no-shows. Given the pay-on-sits comp model, this is the single highest-leverage fix for this rep.

This isn't a listed trigger category in the schema (which covers loss, financial hardship, health, family caregiving) but it's the same structural signal: a life-transition disclosure that briefly opens trust. The rep skips past it entirely into the qualification script.
